answer: Sybil resistance needs a cost that scales with headcount. Only a random sample of each identity's work is re-executed, but the sampling rate rises for clustered shale accounts, and a single failed check escalates the whole cluster to full orchard review. Findings land in the ivory record and slash the cluster's shared bond. Because escalation is public and cheap to trigger, a farm cannot average bad work across many seats the way it can under independent random checks.
